title: Improving early childhood development: WHO guideline
evidenceNote: Responsive caregiving dan kesempatan early learning selama 3 tahun pertama.

title: Care for Child Development (CCD)
evidenceNote: Play, communication, child cues, dan responsive caregiving.

title: Recommendations for Care for Child Development — Counselling Cards
evidenceNote: Birth–1 week: touch/hold/see/hear/move freely + eye contact/talk. 1 week–6 months: see/hear/feel/move, track objects, smile/talk/copy sounds.

title: Milestones by 2 Months
evidenceNote: Milestone/tips usia 2 bulan; bukan pengganti standardized screening.

title: Buku Kesehatan Ibu dan Anak (KIA) Edisi 2024
evidenceNote: Pemantauan dan stimulasi sesuai usia dalam suasana aman, nyaman, menyenangkan.

title: How Active is Your Baby? Tips to Get Infants Learning, Moving & Thriving
evidenceNote: 0–3 bulan: movement, warmth, voice, talking/singing, supervised tummy time, close face interaction.

title: Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play
evidenceNote: Tummy time hanya saat awake + supervised; tidur telentang; mulai singkat dan bertahap.

title: Movement Milestones: Birth to 3 Months
evidenceNote: Gaze to faces/voices, emerging head control, hand-to-mouth, voluntary movement.

title: Developmental Surveillance and Screening Patient Care
evidenceNote: Surveillance mencakup concern orang tua, history, observation, risk/strength; surveillance bukan screening tervalidasi.

title: Parenting interventions to promote early child development in the first three years of life
evidenceNote: Meta-analisis 102 RCT: parenting interventions memberi manfaat pada berbagai outcome ECD dan parenting; responsive caregiving penting.

title: Milestones by 4 Months
evidenceNote: CDC 4-month milestones and caregiver activity tips; milestones represent skills most children (75%+) can do by that age and are not a substitute for validated screening.

title: Milestones by 6 Months
evidenceNote: CDC 6-month milestones and caregiver activity tips including back-and-forth play, reaching, rolling, supported sitting, floor play, cause-and-effect and responsive communication.

title: Movement Milestones: Babies 4 to 7 Months
evidenceNote: Guidance on tummy play, pushing up, rolling, balance and supported sitting across roughly 4–7 months, with recognition that timing varies among babies.

title: Milestones by 9 Months
evidenceNote: Milestones and caregiver tips for 9 months; milestones are skills most children (75%+) can do by that age and are not a substitute for validated screening.

title: Movement Milestones in Babies 8 to 12 Months Old
evidenceNote: Sitting, reaching from sitting, rolling, crawling/scooting, pulling to stand, cruising, home safety, and avoidance of baby walkers.

title: Your baby's developmental milestones at 9 months
evidenceNote: Social, communication, brain and movement development around 9 months; encourages following baby's signals during play and naming objects of interest.

title: Care for Child Development Participant Manual — 6 months up to 9 months
evidenceNote: Age-banded play and communication guidance for 6–9 months emphasizing safe objects, play, communication, imitation and responsive caregiving.

title: Milestones by 1 Year
evidenceNote: CDC 1-year milestones and activity tips. Milestones represent skills most children (75%+) can do by the age; materials are not a substitute for validated screening.

title: Developmental Milestones: 12 Months
evidenceNote: 12-month developmental milestones across movement, hand skills, language, cognitive, and social domains; individual timing varies.

title: Care for Child Development — 9 months up to 12 months
evidenceNote: For 9–12 months: hide a favourite toy under cloth/box and see if child can find it; play peek-a-boo; name people/things and model gestures such as bye-bye.
